site.title: Echelon | Interschool tech fest at Bangalore International School
site.description: Echelon 4.0 at Bangalore International School: eight interschool technology events for Grades 8–12 on the theme Small Steps, Big Impact, in collaboration with Vidyashilp University.

event.name: Echelon
event.tagline: Like migrating birds, we rise in formation.
event.summary: Small Steps, Big Impact. Eight events for Grades 8–12 to code, build, pitch and race, in collaboration with Vidyashilp University. Interpret this year’s theme creatively and make your ideas count.
event._dateHelp: Set date to an ISO date with the India offset, for example 2027-01-16T08:30:00+05:30. Leave it empty to show 'Date to be announced'.

about.heading: Teamwork that takes us further
paragraphs: Echelon is the V-shaped formation birds use when migrating. Birds at the back conserve energy before taking their turn to lead the pack. This teamwork is what we hope students will emulate through Echelon, our technology fest.

The theme for every event this year is “Small Steps, Big Impact”. Interpret it any way you want—be creative. Students in Grades 8–12 come together at Bangalore International School, in collaboration with Vidyashilp University, to turn small ideas into meaningful results.

name.heading: Every letter stands for something
name._help: From the official Echelon logo. Keep one word per letter of ECHELON, in order; the build checks this. The same words are drawn around the logo in src/logo.js (WORDS).

cards.title: Eight ways to compete
cards.text: Escape a locked room, find treasure, design websites and games, build with e-waste, race drones, pitch innovations and create an expert system in SWI-Prolog.

cards.title: Teams from your school
cards.text: Like migrating birds sharing the lead, work together, support your teammates and build on one another’s ideas.

cards.title: One day on campus
cards.text: Everything happens at Bangalore International School, from 8:15 am to 2:30 pm. Breakfast and lunch are provided.

steps.title: Choose your challenge
steps.text: Explore eight events on “Small Steps, Big Impact”. Seven start at 9:30 am; Treasure Hunt starts at 10:15 am. Check overlapping times before choosing your events.

steps.title: Team up and register
steps.text: Form a team of three and register on the official form. Each school can enter up to two teams per event.

steps.title: Prepare your materials
steps.text: Check your event’s rules and equipment. Save Web Designing files locally and bring e-waste or a drone if required. For Pitch Tank, bring your device on the day or email the presentation before 19 November 2026.

steps.title: Check in and compete
steps.text: Report by 8:15 am for registration and breakfast. Attend the 9:00 am opening, then head to your event’s room. Competitions finish by 12:15 pm; lunch is at 12:45 pm and prizes at 1:30 pm.

events.heading: Eight events. Pick yours.
events.intro: This year’s theme for all events is “Small Steps, Big Impact”. Interpret it creatively. Check each event’s time, room, preparation and rules below.

items.name: Escape Room – Code Breakers
items.summary: Escape the locked room: trace Python, Java or pseudocode to unlock the safe.
items.priorKnowledge: Trace tables; Python, Java or pseudocode
about: Trace the code and work out its output using trace tables.
Use Python, Java or pseudocode to solve the challenges and unlock the safe.

items.name: Treasure Hunt – Logic & Discovery
items.summary: Find the checkpoints, solve the puzzles and find the treasure!
items.venue: Starts in the First Floor CS Lab
items.priorKnowledge: Simple decryption, puzzle-solving, mathematical reasoning and graphing tasks may be required
about: Start in the first-floor CS Lab and follow the checkpoints.
Solve puzzles and uncover clues to reach the treasure.

items.name: Web Designing
items.summary: Code a website on this year’s theme, “Small Steps, Big Impact”.
items.resources: Save all required files locally before the competition starts
about: Code a website on “Small Steps, Big Impact” using HTML and scripting languages.
Interpret the theme creatively and build your website from scratch.
rules: No templates or AI tools are permitted.
Internet access will be disabled during the competition.
Save all required files locally before starting.

items.name: Game Designing
items.summary: Create a game on this year’s theme, “Small Steps, Big Impact”.
items.priorKnowledge: Your chosen software or programming language, such as Scratch or Python
items.resources: Bring your laptop or use the Windows PCs provided
about: Create a game on “Small Steps, Big Impact”. Interpret the theme creatively.
Any software or programming language is permitted, including Scratch or Python.
Demonstrate your game, and explain its code, logic and how it works, to the assessment panel.
rules: Bring your laptop or use the Windows PCs provided.

items.name: E-Waste Reimagined – Product Design
items.summary: Create a reusable product using e-waste, with all work done during the competition.
about: Build a sustainable, useful or innovative reusable product from e-waste.
Connect your idea to “Small Steps, Big Impact”.
rules: All work must be completed during the competition.
Products are judged on creativity, usefulness, sustainability and how well you use your materials.

items.name: Drone Racing – Precision Challenge
items.summary: Navigate your drone through a challenging obstacle course!
items.resources: Bring your own drone and batteries; drones and batteries will not be provided
about: Navigate your drone through the obstacle course.
Show precision and control as you tackle each obstacle.
rules: Bring your own drone. Multiple teams may share a drone.
Drones must be no larger than 30 cm × 30 cm and must weigh under 250 g.
Drones and batteries will not be provided.
Do not use damaged batteries. Use propeller guards.

items.name: Pitch Tank – Innovation Pitch
items.summary: Pitch your innovative solutions to real-world problems to our judges!
items.resources: Bring your device or email your presentation to mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026
about: Pitch an innovative solution to a real-world problem.
Explain your idea and how it can make a meaningful impact.
rules: Each presentation has a five-minute limit.
AI is permitted during the development phase.
Bring your device or email your presentation to mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence – Prolog Expert System Challenge
items.summary: Design a knowledge-based expert system using SWI-Prolog.
items.venue: First Floor AI and Robotics Lab
about: Design a knowledge-based expert system using SWI-Prolog.
Apply your prior knowledge of SWI-Prolog to build and demonstrate your system.
rules: Prior knowledge of SWI-Prolog is required.
Systems are assessed on the accuracy and relevance of their facts, the correctness of their rules, how well they infer conclusions from queries, and how well your team understands the logic.
Be ready to demonstrate your program and explain how your expert system works to the assessment panel.

schedule.heading: The event-day flow
schedule.intro: Seven events begin at 9:30 am; Treasure Hunt starts at 10:15 am. Follow the timeline for event finishes, lunch and prizes.

before.title: Register your teams
before.text: Sign up on the official registration form.

before.title: Prepare your Pitch Tank presentation
before.text: Bring your device on the day or email your presentation to mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026. AI is permitted during development; each presentation lasts five minutes.

day.title: Reporting, registration and breakfast
day.text: Check in and have breakfast before the 9:00 am opening ceremony.

day.title: Opening ceremony
day.text: Echelon 4.0 opens. Get ready to explore “Small Steps, Big Impact”.

day.title: Seven events begin
day.text: Escape Room: First Floor CS Lab. Web and Game Designing: Ground Floor CS Lab. AI: First Floor AI and Robotics Lab. Pitch Tank: Second Floor AV Room. E-Waste Reimagined: First Floor AV Room. Drone Racing: Fifth Floor AV Room.

day.title: Treasure Hunt begins
day.text: Start in the First Floor CS Lab. Find checkpoints and solve puzzles until 10:45 am.

day.title: Web and Game Designing finish
day.text: Both two-hour design events finish in the Ground Floor CS Lab.

day.title: AI, Pitch Tank and E-Waste finish
day.text: The expert-system, innovation-pitch and e-waste events conclude.

day.title: Drone Racing finishes
day.text: The final competition ends in the Fifth Floor AV Room.

items.q: How big is a team, and how many can a school send?
items.a: Every team has three students, and each school can enter up to two teams in each event.
AI tools are not permitted in Web Designing or Game Designing. Pitch Tank permits AI during the development phase. Web Designing also prohibits templates and has no internet access.
On Saturday, 21 November 2026, at Bangalore International School. Report by 8:15 am. The day ends with prize distribution, from 1:30 to 2:30 pm.
Yes. Breakfast (8:15 to 9:00 am) and lunch (12:45 to 1:20 pm) are provided.

Web Designing: save all required files locally before starting; internet will be disabled. Game Designing: bring your laptop or use the Windows PCs provided. E-Waste Reimagined: bring your own e-waste and complete all work during the competition. Drone Racing: bring your drone and batteries; the drone must be at most 30 × 30 cm and under 250 g. Use propeller guards and do not use damaged batteries. Teams may share drones. Pitch Tank: bring your device or email your presentation to mahenthren@bischool.in before 19 November 2026.

items.q: Who do we contact with questions?
items.a: Email the organising team at malarvizhi@bischool.in.
